sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是99%隐形播客。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: Off the east coast of mainland Canada is the island of Newfoundland.
sentences.zh: 在加拿大本土东海岸外，是纽芬兰岛。

sentences.en: The island is as far east as you can go and still be in Canada.
sentences.zh: 这座岛屿是身处加拿大时所能到达的最东端。

sentences.en: So far east, in fact, that it has its own time zone.
sentences.zh: 事实上，它位于如此靠东的地方，以至于它拥有自己的时区。

sentences.en: A half an hour later than anywhere else in North America.
sentences.zh: 比北美其他任何地方都晚半个小时。

sentences.en: If you've seen a photograph of the island, it's probably the one that went viral last year
sentences.zh: 如果你看过一张关于这座岛的照片，那很可能就是去年在网上疯传的那张

sentences.en: of a small village on the eastern coaSt.
sentences.zh: 展示东海岸一个小村庄的照片。

sentences.en: In the foreground are rolling hills and a couple of houses.
sentences.zh: 前景中是起伏的丘陵和几栋房子。

sentences.en: In the background, a gigantic iceberg floats by on the choppy blue sea.
sentences.zh: 背景中，一座巨大的冰山漂过波涛汹涌的蓝色海洋。

sentences.en: Yeah, icebergs float by occasionally, but that one was actually scary big.
sentences.zh: 是的，冰山偶尔会漂过，但那座大得确实有点吓人。

sentences.en: And nice pronunciation of Newfoundland, by the way.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，你对纽芬兰的发音很不错。

sentences.en: A lot of people say Newfoundland, and it's a bit of a sore spot with us locals.
sentences.zh: 很多人把纽芬兰的发音读错，这对我们当地人来说是个有点敏感的话题。

sentences.en: That is Newfoundland native Luke Quinton.
sentences.zh: 那是纽芬兰本地人卢克·奎顿。

sentences.en: And I want to take us to a different part of the island,
sentences.zh: 我想带大家去岛上的另一个地方，

sentences.en: to a little town on the northeastern side called Gander.
sentences.zh: 去东北部一个叫甘德的小镇。

sentences.en: Now, looking back, I was all of 20 years old at the time, though I thought I was ancient.
sentences.zh: 现在回想起来，当时我整整20岁，虽然我自以为已经老气横秋了。

sentences.en: It's Christmas Eve, 1972, and Ian Blackmore is working.
sentences.zh: 那是1972年的平安夜，伊恩·布莱克莫尔正在工作。

sentences.en: My name is Ian Blackmore, and I was a photographer with the Gander beacon
sentences.zh: 我叫伊恩·布莱克莫尔，我曾是《甘德灯塔报》的摄影师，

sentences.en: after I finished high school and before I went to college in Toronto.
sentences.zh: 那是在我高中毕业之后、去多伦多上大学之前。

sentences.en: Ian's co-worker, Gerald Vokey, was an editor on the same local paper.
sentences.zh: 伊恩的同事杰拉尔德·沃基是这家当地报纸的编辑。

sentences.en: He's going to help tell this story.
sentences.zh: 他将协助讲述这个故事。

sentences.en: It was Christmas Eve, and her mother was, you know, getting things ready for Santa Claus.
sentences.zh: 那是平安夜，她的母亲，你知道的，正在为圣诞老人做准备。

sentences.en: Gerald was home that day in 1972.
sentences.zh: 1972年的那天，杰拉尔德在家。

sentences.en: His family was getting ready for Christmas, and he wanted to get his daughter out of the house.
sentences.zh: 他的家人正在筹备圣诞节，他想把女儿带出家门。

sentences.en: So they decided to go hang out at the local airport.
sentences.zh: 所以他们决定去当地的机场闲逛。

sentences.en: As you do.
sentences.zh: 就像你常做的那样。

sentences.en: As you do when you live in a tiny town in Canada, and the airport is the best thing around.
sentences.zh: 就像你住在加拿大一个小镇上、而机场是方圆百里最好的去处时会做的那样。

sentences.en: Also, this is not a normal airport, but we'll get to that soon.
sentences.zh: 另外，这可不是个普通的机场，不过我们马上就会讲到这一点。

sentences.en: You never knew with the airport being up there who might come through at any given time,
sentences.zh: 因为机场就在那儿，你永远不知道任何时候会有什么人经过，

sentences.en: regardless of the hour of the day or night or whatever.
sentences.zh: 无论是一天中的哪个时间还是夜晚。

sentences.en: And when Gerald got to the Gander airport, he started asking around.
sentences.zh: 当杰拉尔德到达甘德机场时，他开始到处打听。

sentences.en: I asked the security there, you know, what was going on.
sentences.zh: 我问那里的安保人员，你知道的，发生了什么事。

sentences.en: And they said, Fidel Castro is here.
sentences.zh: 他们说，菲德尔·卡斯特罗在这里。

sentences.en: And I said, what?
sentences.zh: 我说，什么？

sentences.en: Fidel Castro was there in the airport, and he was more or less just hanging out.
sentences.zh: 菲德尔·卡斯特罗当时就在机场里，他基本上就是在那儿闲逛。

sentences.en: I had dinner with him.
sentences.zh: 我和他一起吃了晚饭。

sentences.en: Yeah, in the, well, the dining room, naturally.
sentences.zh: 是的，在那个，嗯，餐厅里，很自然地。

sentences.en: He had on his traditional fatigues in his combat boots.
sentences.zh: 他穿着传统的野战服和作战靴。

sentences.en: Green.
sentences.zh: 绿色的。

sentences.en: Green fatigues, no medals or nothing, just plain uniform.
sentences.zh: 绿色野战服，没有勋章什么的，只是普通的制服。

sentences.en: Turned out Castro had a pretty long layover in Gander.
sentences.zh: 原来卡斯特罗在甘德有一个相当长的中转停留。

sentences.en: So at some point, he basically says, give me a tour of your town.
sentences.zh: 所以在某个时刻，他基本上说，带我参观一下你们的小镇吧。

sentences.en: He wanted to see the town.
sentences.zh: 他想看看这个小镇。

sentences.en: So Ian and Gerald and Fidel Castro all pile in some cars and go driving around the little
sentences.zh: 于是伊恩、杰拉尔德和菲德尔·卡斯特罗一起挤进几辆车里，在这个小镇四处兜风，

sentences.en: town until they come across a kid sledding.
sentences.zh: 直到他们遇到一个正在玩雪橇的孩子。

sentences.en: There was a young fellow with his dog and probably another friend there, and they were taking
sentences.zh: 有一个年轻小伙子带着他的狗，可能还有另一个朋友在那里，他们

sentences.en: turns going down on their toboggan.
sentences.zh: 轮流坐着雪橇滑下去。

sentences.en: And, of course, Mr. Castro decided that that looked interesting and figured he might see
sentences.zh: 当然，卡斯特罗先生觉得这看起来很有趣，心想他也许可以看看

sentences.en: what the thing was and how it worked, not being that familiar with snow.
sentences.zh: 这东西是什么以及它是怎么运作的，因为他对雪并不是那么熟悉。

sentences.en: Castro gets on this sled and starts down the hill, and Ian Blackmore snaps a picture.
sentences.zh: 卡斯特罗坐上这个雪橇，开始顺着山坡滑下，伊恩·布莱克莫尔抓拍了一张照片。

sentences.en: I got ahead of him before he started on the slide down, so I was in position for to catch
sentences.zh: 在他开始向下滑之前我跑到了他前面，所以我占好了位置，

sentences.en: him on his way down and, well, photograph him.
sentences.zh: 以便在他滑下来时抓拍他，嗯，给他拍照。

sentences.en: I didn't catch him.
sentences.zh: 我没有拍到他摔倒。

sentences.en: Ian Blackmore's photograph of Fidel Castro sledding would end up in Time magazine.
sentences.zh: 伊恩·布莱克莫尔拍摄的菲德尔·卡斯特罗滑雪橇的照片最终登上了《时代》杂志。

sentences.en: And the amazing thing about this anecdote isn't how unique it was for Gander, but how totally
sentences.zh: 这个轶事神奇的地方不在于它对甘德而言是多么独一无二，而在于它是多么的

sentences.en: normal.
sentences.zh: 稀松平常。

sentences.en: The Gander Airport was used to hosting really famous people from all over the world.
sentences.zh: 甘德机场过去常常接待来自世界各地的真正名流。

sentences.en: It wasn't just some tiny airport in some tiny town.
sentences.zh: 它不只是某个小镇上的某个微型机场。

sentences.en: It was a very large, very important airport in some tiny town.
sentences.zh: 它是某个小镇上一个非常大型、非常重要的机场。

sentences.en: But before we hear how this place came to be, I want to take you inside the airport, because
sentences.zh: 但在我们听闻这个地方是如何诞生之前，我想带你走进机场内部，因为

sentences.en: it's an incredible building.
sentences.zh: 它是一座令人难以置信的建筑。

sentences.en: Okay, here on the Gander Airport.
sentences.zh: 好的，现在来到甘德机场。

sentences.en: The Gander Airport is such a mid-century modern time capsule that I actually think I have to
sentences.zh: 甘德机场是一个如此具有世纪中期现代主义风格的时间胶囊，以至于我甚至觉得现在就得

sentences.en: bring up some lounge music right now.
sentences.zh: 放点休闲音乐来烘托气氛。

sentences.en: This place is straight out of an episode of Mad Men.
sentences.zh: 这个地方简直就像是美剧《广告狂人》里的一集。

sentences.en: You know, Mad Men with Newfoundlander accents.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，带有纽芬兰口音的《广告狂人》。

sentences.en: If you follow me across here, over on the apron.
sentences.zh: 如果你跟我从这里穿过去，来到停机坪上。

sentences.en: Jerry Cram is a commissioner at the Gander Airport.
sentences.zh: 杰里·克拉姆是甘德机场的一名专员。

sentences.en: The job is part fixer, part security guard.
sentences.zh: 这份工作部分是老练的协调员，部分是保安。

sentences.en: Jerry will probably be the one to give you a tour, if you ask.
sentences.zh: 如果你要求的话，杰里很可能会带你参观。

sentences.en: The terrace flooring is all from Italy.
sentences.zh: 露台的地板全部来自意大利。

sentences.en: Right here is what we call the birds of welcome.
sentences.zh: 就在这里，这就是我们所说的迎宾之鸟。

sentences.en: Jerry is pointing at a bronze sculpture of seven birds that greets you when you walk into the lounge.
sentences.zh: 杰里正指着一座七只鸟的青铜雕塑，当你走进休息室时，它会迎接你。

sentences.en: The blue and the gray furniture is all from the late 50s, early 60s.
sentences.zh: 蓝色和灰色的家具全部来自50年代末、60年代初。

sentences.en: The international lounge of the Gander Airport is this big, airy space, super high ceilings, and when you walk in, you're immediately awash in the orangey glow of the 1950s.
sentences.zh: 甘德机场的国际休息室是一个宽敞、通风的空间，拥有超高的天花板，当你走进去时，你立即会被20世纪50年代的橙色光芒所笼罩。

sentences.en: The vinyl chairs and couches are arranged in U-shaped seating areas.
sentences.zh: 乙烯基材质的椅子和沙发被安排在U型的休息区里。

sentences.en: They were designed by famous mid-century designers like Charles and Ray Eames and Robin Bush.
sentences.zh: 它们是由世纪中叶的著名设计师设计的，如查尔斯和雷·埃姆斯以及罗宾·布什。

sentences.en: The Gander International Lounge has been called the single most important modernist room in Canada.
sentences.zh: 甘德国际休息室被称为加拿大最单体最重要的现代主义房间。

sentences.en: Even the bathrooms are their own amazing time capsule.
sentences.zh: 甚至连洗手间本身都是一个令人惊叹的时间胶囊。

sentences.en: The women's restroom especially.
sentences.zh: 尤其是女洗手间。

sentences.en: Jerry calls out a warning so that we can go in.
sentences.zh: 杰里大声发出警告，以便我们能够进去。

sentences.en: Mail guard!
sentences.zh: 男士回避！

sentences.en: This is not a gross airport bathroom.
sentences.zh: 这不是一个令人恶心的机场厕所。

sentences.en: It's beautiful, mid-century luxury.
sentences.zh: 它是美丽的中世纪奢华。

sentences.en: There's a row of swivel chairs in front of a counter and a wall-sized mirror.
sentences.zh: 柜台前有一排转椅和一面墙大小的镜子。

sentences.en: It has two showers because, yes, people used to shower at the airport.
sentences.zh: 它有两个淋浴间，因为，是的，人们过去常常在机场洗澡。

sentences.en: Well, there is two showers in this room as well as in the men's.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这个房间里有两个淋浴间，男士洗手间里也有。

sentences.en: But now you can say you were in the washroom that the queen peppered her nose in on June the 19th, 1959.
sentences.zh: 但现在你可以说，你曾去过英国女王在1959年6月19日补过妆的洗手间。

sentences.en: When this international lounge of the Gander Airport opened in 1959, the Queen of England herself came for the opening.
sentences.zh: 当甘德机场的这个国际休息室于1959年开放时，英国女王本人亲自出席了开幕式。

sentences.en: And yeah, the townspeople popped up with her, too.
sentences.zh: 而且是的，镇民们也和她一起出现了。

sentences.en: A lot has happened in this airport.
sentences.zh: 这个机场发生过很多事情。

sentences.en: And the story of how it came to be and what it's become is really also a story about the history of air travel.
sentences.zh: 它如何诞生以及它变成了什么的故事，其实也是一部航空旅行的发展史。

sentences.en: Why Newfoundland?
sentences.zh: 为什么是纽芬兰？

sentences.en: Because it's the shortest way.
sentences.zh: 因为这是最近的路。

sentences.en: Come here, let me show you.
sentences.zh: 过来，我给你看看。

sentences.en: You've got to look at it on a globe.
sentences.zh: 你得在地球仪上看它。

sentences.en: If you trace a direct course from New York to Paris, you'll see that it takes you right over Newfoundland.
sentences.zh: 如果你画一条从纽约到巴黎的直线航线，你会发现它正好经过纽芬兰上空。

sentences.en: Remember, Lindbergh went this way, and he didn't have any guess.
sentences.zh: 记住，林德伯格就是走这条路的，而且他没有任何猜测。

sentences.en: In the 1920s, before Gander existed, Newfoundland's grassy fields were the jumping-off points for transatlantic daredevil pilots.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪20年代甘德存在之前，纽芬兰的长满青草的田野是跨大西洋勇敢飞行员的跳板。

sentences.en: Amelia Earhart, Alcock & Brown, Lindbergh, all of them.
sentences.zh: 阿梅莉亚·埃尔哈特、奥尔科特和布朗、林德伯格，所有人都是如此。

sentences.en: Because it was so far east, it made sense to start there if you were worried about getting across the Atlantic with enough fuel.
sentences.zh: 因为它如此靠东，如果你担心带着足够的燃料飞越大西洋，从那里出发就很有意义。

sentences.en: Eventually, the British government, which controlled Newfoundland at the time, started to take note.
sentences.zh: 最终，当时控制纽芬兰的英国政府开始注意到这一点。

sentences.en: Maybe there was something to this whole air travel thing.
sentences.zh: 也许这整个航空旅行的事情真有什么门道。

sentences.en: In 1936, the British chose what was then basically a patch of woods on the eastern side of Newfoundland as the site for over a million square yards of runways.
sentences.zh: 1936年，英国人将当时基本上是纽芬兰东部的一片树林选为超过一百万平方码跑道的建设地点。

sentences.en: By the spring of 1938, the Gander Airport was fully operational, but the massive runways were mostly unused.
sentences.zh: 到1938年春天，甘德机场已全面投入运营，但庞大的跑道大多闲置不用。

sentences.en: There just weren't enough planes in operation that could actually survive the crossing of the Atlantic Ocean.
sentences.zh: 当时运营的飞机根本不够多，无法真正挺过横跨大西洋的飞行。

sentences.en: It was a very, very risky journey.
sentences.zh: 那是一次非常非常危险的旅程。

sentences.en: In the two decades before the war, only 100 planes had crossed the Atlantic.
sentences.zh: 在战争爆发前的二十年里，只有100架飞机飞越大西洋。

sentences.en: 50 others had tried and failed.
sentences.zh: 另外50架尝试过但失败了。

sentences.en: 40 people had died.
sentences.zh: 40人丧生。

sentences.en: Then in 1939, World War II began in Europe, and Allied forces wanted as many fighter planes as they could get their hands on.
sentences.zh: 然后在1939年，第二次世界大战在欧洲爆发，盟军想要尽可能多的战斗机。

sentences.en: Americans and Canadians had been shipping planes over by boat, but that wasn't working out so well.
sentences.zh: 美国人和加拿大人一直通过船只运送飞机，但这并不太管用。

sentences.en: They were being torpedoed by German submarines and whatnot, so they were losing more airplanes than were actually making it over to the UK.
sentences.zh: 它们遭到德国潜水艇等的鱼雷攻击，因此损失的飞机比实际成功运抵英国的飞机还要多。

sentences.en: That's historian and former air dispatcher Dean Cull.
sentences.zh: 那是历史学家兼前空中调度员迪安·卡尔。

sentences.en: And he says to get planes to the UK, the British had to come up with a new idea.
sentences.zh: 他说，为了将飞机运送到英国，英国人不得不提出一个新想法。

sentences.en: They would have to put what we call a bladder inside.
sentences.zh: 他们必须在里面安装我们所说的气囊。

sentences.en: It was a spare fuel tank, basically, to give them enough fuel to make the crossing.
sentences.zh: 基本上是一个备用油箱，为它们提供足够的燃料来完成飞行。

sentences.en: The process of flying the planes from Gander to Scotland began in 1940 and was called the Ferry Command.
sentences.zh: 将飞机从甘德飞往苏格兰的过程始于1940年，被称为渡运司令部。

sentences.en: The first crossing was seven planes, and it took place on a freezing night in November.
sentences.zh: 第一次飞行有七架飞机，发生在一个寒风刺骨的11月夜晚。

sentences.en: The pilots had to fly in the dark because lights could alert the Germans.
sentences.zh: 飞行员必须在黑暗中飞行，因为灯光可能会惊动德国人。

sentences.en: Miraculously, all seven made it.
sentences.zh: 奇迹般的是，所有七架飞机都成功抵达。

sentences.en: But that was just the first day.
sentences.zh: 但这只是第一天。

sentences.en: Over the course of the war, 20,000 planes were brought to Gander to be flown across the Atlantic for the war.
sentences.zh: 在战争期间，有2万架飞机被带到甘德，以便飞越大西洋参加战争。

sentences.en: Some days there would be 100 airplanes that would go over.
sentences.zh: 有时一天会有100架飞机飞过。

sentences.en: And Churchill was even quoted at one point.
sentences.zh: 丘吉尔甚至在某次发言中被引用过。

sentences.en: And he referred to Gander as the largest aircraft carrier in the North Atlantic.
sentences.zh: 他把甘德称为北大西洋上最大的航空母舰。

sentences.en: I guess it was the turning point of the war, really, for Britain.
sentences.zh: 我想这确实是英国战争的转折点。

sentences.en: Gander was making history, even though at the time there was no actual town of Gander.
sentences.zh: 甘德在创造历史，尽管当时并没有真正意义上的甘德镇。

sentences.en: There was no town.
sentences.zh: 当时没有城镇。

sentences.en: There were people living between intersections of runways.
sentences.zh: 人们住在跑道交叉口之间。

sentences.en: And that's where the Americans and the Canadians and the British had built wartime buildings.
sentences.zh: 那就是美国人、加拿大人和英国人建造战时建筑的地方。

sentences.en: Frank Dubow is a former air traffic controller at Gander and historian of the airport.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克·杜博w是甘德的前空中交通管制员兼机场历史学家。

sentences.en: And he says the early town of Gander was basically just a few living quarters right next to the runways.
sentences.zh: 他说早期的甘德镇基本上只是紧挨着跑道的几处起居室。

sentences.en: I would say, you know, 100 yards or so, or even closer than that.
sentences.zh: 我想说，你知道的，大约100码左右，甚至比那还要近。

sentences.en: And they made a hell of a lot of noise, those aircraft.
sentences.zh: 那些飞机制造了巨大的噪音。

sentences.en: Because the Gander airport started as a military operation,
sentences.zh: 因为甘德机场最初是一项军事行动，

sentences.en: it wasn't until the war was over and civilian air travel began
sentences.zh: 直到战争结束、民用航空开始之后，

sentences.en: that they decided to build a separate town away from the runways.
sentences.zh: 他们才决定在远离跑道的地方建立一个独立的城镇。
